title: Implant-Supported Bridges
meta_title: Implant-Supported Bridges in Alexandria | West Alexandria Dental Care
meta_description: Replacing several teeth in a row on two or more implants: how it differs from a traditional bridge, planning with 3D imaging, the timeline.
intro: When three or four teeth in a row are missing, you do not need an implant for every one. Two or more implants can carry a bridge across the whole gap, with no natural teeth ground down to hold it and the bone beneath kept in use. It is the usual answer for a longer gap when the neighbors are sound.

sections.heading: Implant bridge or traditional bridge?
rows: Crowns on the natural teeth either side
Kept in use by the implants
Can replace three, four or more teeth
Limited; long spans overload the anchors

sections.heading: Why fewer implants than teeth
body: An implant can carry more than one tooth. For a gap of three teeth, two implants at either end support a three-unit bridge with the middle tooth suspended between them. For four or more, three implants may be used. The number and position are worked out from the 3D scan: where the bone is, where the chewing forces will fall, and how to avoid the nerve and sinus. Fewer implants means less surgery and lower cost without compromising strength, provided the planning is right.
When there is a natural tooth at one end of the gap and nothing at the other, an implant bridge also avoids the cantilever that a traditional bridge would need.

items.title: Planning
items.body: A cone-beam CT scan and models of your teeth. The implant positions are planned to support the bridge evenly and to sit in solid bone. Grafting is discussed if needed.

items.title: Placement
items.body: The implants are placed in one visit under local anesthetic, with sedation options after review if you want them. A temporary bridge or partial can fill a visible gap during healing.

items.title: Healing
items.body: Three to six months while the bone fuses to the implants.

items.title: Impression and laboratory
items.body: The implant positions are recorded precisely and the bridge is made in ceramic, often on a strong internal framework, to match the surrounding teeth.

items.title: Fitting
items.body: The bridge is tried in, the fit and bite checked, and it is screwed or cemented onto the implants. Screw-retained bridges can be removed by us for maintenance if ever needed.

sections.heading: When it is the right choice
items: Three or more adjacent teeth are missing and the neighbors are healthy.
The gap is at the back of the mouth with no tooth behind it.
A traditional bridge would overload the remaining teeth.
You want a fixed replacement rather than a removable partial.
Bone is adequate, or can be built up, where the implants would go.

sections.heading: Caring for an implant bridge
body: The bridge is cleaned like a natural bridge: brush all surfaces, and clean under the suspended teeth and around each implant daily with floss threaders, interdental brushes or a water flosser. The implants do not decay, but the gum around them can become inflamed if plaque collects, so regular professional cleanings matter. A night guard is recommended for anyone who grinds. The [aftercare page](/dental-implants/aftercare/) has the detail.

sections.heading: Cost, in general terms
sections.body: An implant bridge costs more than a traditional bridge or a partial denture and less than one implant per missing tooth. Insurance coverage varies widely and is checked before you commit; you receive a written estimate for the full sequence at the planning visit.

faqs.q: How many implants will I need?
faqs.a: Usually two for three missing teeth, and two or three for four or more. The 3D scan and the chewing forces involved decide it, and the plan is explained before anything is placed.

faqs.q: Can an implant bridge replace all the teeth in an arch?
faqs.a: Yes. A full arch can be supported on four to six implants as a fixed bridge. That is a larger undertaking, planned the same way, and we discuss it alongside implant-retained dentures as an alternative.
Not by you. A screw-retained bridge can be removed by the dentist for cleaning or repair, which is one of its advantages.

faqs.q: How long will it take from start to finish?
faqs.a: Four to eight months, depending on healing time and whether any grafting is needed. A temporary keeps a visible gap filled throughout.

cta.heading: Several teeth, a few implants, nothing ground down.
cta.body: Book a consultation and a 3D scan. We will show you how many implants the gap needs and what the finished bridge involves.
